transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm here because I really need help. There is a group of people who have been following me and monitoring everything I do, and I don't feel safe anymore. I know they are targeting me, and I just need someone to believe me.
Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of depression or episodes of elevated mood or irritability, along with these feelings of being followed?

No, my mood has been completely normal, and I don't feel depressed or anything like that. The only issue is that these people are constantly watching me and tracking my movements. That is my main concern because it's happening every single day.
Aside from feeling like you're being followed, have you experienced any unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot?
No, I definitely don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. Everything I'm experiencing with these people is completely real and happening in the physical world.
How long have you been experiencing the feeling of being followed and monitored by this group of people?

It has been going on for about three months now. I first noticed them tracking me back in November, and it has been happening every single day since then. I'm just so anxious and exhausted because I never know what they are planning to do to me.
Have you noticed any changes in your thoughts, such as difficulty concentrating, or changes in your behavior, such as social withdrawal, since you started feeling like you're being followed?

My concentration and thinking are completely fine, and I can focus on my work just like before. However, I have had to change my behavior and stay indoors a lot more, avoiding certain places and people just to keep myself safe from them. Other than taking those safety precautions to avoid being monitored, my daily life and functioning are completely normal.
Are the people you believe are following you targeting you specifically, or is it more of a general feeling of being monitored, and do you think this is due to something you've done or who you are?

They are absolutely targeting me specifically; it's not just a general feeling at all. I know it is a group from a local organization that has been tracking my exact movements because of some important research I've been working on. They want to steal my findings, and it makes me incredibly anxious to know they are constantly watching my every move.
Can you tell me more about this research you've been working on and why you think it's so important that this group would go to such great lengths to steal it?

I have developed a revolutionary formula that could completely solve the global energy crisis, making it worth billions of dollars. This group knows my findings will change the world, which is why they have tapped my phones and are tracking my every move to steal it. I have to be extremely careful because they will stop at nothing to get their hands on my work.
Do you think your belief about the group following you and trying to steal your research is something that you could be mistaken about, or are you completely convinced that it's true?

I am absolutely certain about this, and there is no way I could be mistaken. It is honestly frustrating to have my reality questioned when I see them tracking me every single day just to steal my energy formula. I know for a fact that this is happening.

Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of depression or episodes of elevated mood or irritability, along with these feelings of being followed, that may have started after the alleged surveillance began?

No, I haven't experienced any major mood swings, depression, or elevated moods. I only feel naturally stressed and anxious because I am constantly being monitored by these people. Other than that normal reaction to the stress, my mood is completely stable.

The patient's delusional belief is non-bizarre (involving situations that occur in real life, such as being followed), and it has been present for more than a month. The absence of significant mood symptoms (depression or mania) and other psychotic symptoms (such as hallucinations) rules out Schizophrenia and Schizoaffective Disorder. The patient's functioning and concentration are relatively preserved outside of the delusional belief, which further supports the diagnosis of Delusional Disorder.
